1.1.evidence:
I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business world and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.
1.1.rationale: The policy explicitly references violence occurring within the household and cites the law on the elimination of domestic violence, indicating domestic violence is within scope.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Seluma Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, so as to cause anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others.
21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
30. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
1.2.rationale: The policy explicitly defines sexual violence and includes it among forms of violence covered.

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 20
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to conduct development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Development as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards.
2.5.rationale: The policy mandates development and supervision activities that include technical guidance and training, which constitutes training/capacity building for implementation actors (e.g., government/service workers).

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Seluma Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, so as to cause anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others.
21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
30. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
